name: Volatility breakout, open + k x prior range, one-day hold (crypto daily)
author: TradingView author (Volatility Breakout Daily)
summary: Buys when price breaks open + K x yesterday's range and exits at the next open; author says it is valid on the Bitcoin daily chart and recommends long only.
notes: Original fills intraday at the trigger and exits next open; here the signal is the daily close beyond the trigger, traded next bar and held one bar (exit always true). Short side not recommended by author, omitted.

name: Larry Williams volatility break-out (stop and reverse)
author: Larry Williams
summary: Long above open + k x prior range, short below open - k x prior range, always in the market; broker claims no losing years in its tests but weak in sideways/low-vol markets.
short_entry: close < open - k * (shift(high,1) - shift(low,1))
notes: Intraday stop fills approximated by daily close beyond the level; position held until the opposite break.

name: Volatility breakout with averaged range and trend side filter
author: LuxAlgo (after Larry Williams)
summary: Variant of the Williams breakout using the average range of the last n sessions and taking only the side agreeing with the higher-timeframe trend; time exit next session.
long_entry: close > open + k * shift(sma(high - low,n),1) & close > sma(close,100)
short_entry: close < open - k * shift(sma(high - low,n),1) & close < sma(close,100)
notes: Page leaves k, n and the trend filter unspecified; trend filter set to SMA(100) by us. One-day hold (exit always true).

name: Crabel opening-range offset breakout (daily approximation)
author: Toby Crabel
summary: Breakout from the open by the 10-day average distance from each open to its nearer extreme, held to the session end.
long_entry: close > open + k * shift(sma(min(high - open, open - low),10),1)
short_entry: close < open - k * shift(sma(min(high - open, open - low),10),1)
notes: Crabel traded intraday stops; daily close used as trigger, one-day hold. Multiplier k not given on the page.

name: Dual Thrust range breakout
author: Michael Chalek (QuantConnect tutorial)
summary: Range = max(HH-LC, HC-LL) over N days; buy above open + K1 x range, sell below open - K2 x range, reversing on the opposite break.
long_entry: close > open + k1 * max(highest(high,n,1) - lowest(close,n,1), highest(close,n,1) - lowest(low,n,1))
long_exit: close < open - k2 * max(highest(high,n,1) - lowest(close,n,1), highest(close,n,1) - lowest(low,n,1))
short_entry: close < open - k2 * max(highest(high,n,1) - lowest(close,n,1), highest(close,n,1) - lowest(low,n,1))
short_exit: close > open + k1 * max(highest(high,n,1) - lowest(close,n,1), highest(close,n,1) - lowest(low,n,1))
notes: Original is intraday with stop orders; daily close used as trigger. Tutorial demo uses K1=K2=0.5.

name: Larry Williams Greatest Swing Value
author: Larry Williams
summary: After down closes, buy a break of open + 1.8 x average up-swing (high-open); after up closes, sell a break of open - 1.8 x average down-swing (open-low).
long_entry: shift(close,1) < shift(close,6) & close > open + f * shift(sma(high - open,4),1)
long_exit: shift(close,1) > shift(close,6) & close < open - f * shift(sma(open - low,4),1)
short_entry: shift(close,1) > shift(close,6) & close < open - f * shift(sma(open - low,4),1)
short_exit: shift(close,1) < shift(close,6) & close > open + f * shift(sma(high - open,4),1)
notes: Williams averages swings only over down (up) days; we average over all of the last 4 days. Trend test = close vs close 5 days earlier (forum). Intraday stop entry approximated by daily close; held until opposite signal.

name: ATR-level breakout (daily approximation of intraday BTC system)
author: Andrea Unger / Unger Academy
summary: Intraday Bitcoin futures breakout at levels derived from ATR away from the prior close.
short_entry: close < shift(close,1) - k * shift(atr(n),1)
notes: Original runs on 5-minute CME bars with session exits; here a daily close beyond the ATR level, held one bar. Exact ATR multiple not disclosed.

name: NR7 buy at close, exit on close above prior high
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Long at the close of a day whose range is the narrowest of the last seven, sell when the close exceeds the prior day's high; tested on SPY since 1993.
notes: Rules as quoted in search snippets of the QS article (full rules paywalled; page says one entry parameter and one exit criterion). Long only.

name: Crabel NR7 bracket breakout
author: Toby Crabel / Quantified Strategies
summary: After an NR7 day, go long above its high or short below its low; QS GLD test: 445 trades, 71% winners, PF 2, CAGR 6.3%, 21% exposure.
short_entry: (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,6,2)) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Exit rules not visible (paywall); we exit on an x-day low/high break as an approximation of the NR7-bar stop. Intraday stop entries approximated by close.

name: NR7 breakout with EMA(20) trend filter
author: Trading Setups Review
summary: Trade the NR7 bar break only when the seven prior bars sit entirely above (long) or below (short) the 20 EMA.
long_entry: lowest(low - ema(close,20),7,1) > 0 & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,6,2)) & close > shift(high,1)
short_entry: highest(high - ema(close,20),7,1) < 0 & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,6,2)) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Source is intraday-oriented with no fixed exit; exit on close back through the EMA(20) chosen by us.

name: NR7 with direction borrowed from higher-timeframe trend
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Systematic NR7 version taking only the bracket side that agrees with a higher-timeframe trend filter.
long_entry: (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,6,2)) & close > shift(high,1) & close > sma(close,200)
short_entry: (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,6,2)) & close < shift(low,1) & close < sma(close,200)
notes: Trend filter chosen as SMA(200); exit on 5-day extreme approximates the opposite-side stop.

name: Inside Day / NR4 breakout (Street Smarts)
author: Linda Bradford Raschke / Laurence Connors
summary: After a day that is both an inside day and the narrowest of 4, buy-stop above its high and sell-stop below its low, with stop-and-reverse.
long_entry: (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2)) & close > shift(high,1)
short_entry: (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2)) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Stop-and-reverse at the setup-bar extreme cannot reference a fixed bar; approximated by x-day low/high exit. Entry on daily close beyond the level.

name: Connors-Raschke historical volatility ratio + ID/NR4 (tested on BTC)
author: CryptoDataDownload (after Connors/Raschke)
summary: Requires 6-day/100-day historical volatility below 50% plus an inside NR4 day, then trades the break of that day's high or low; coded on Binance BTC data.
long_entry: (shift(realized_vol(6) / realized_vol(100),1) < r) & (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2)) & close > shift(high,1)
short_entry: (shift(realized_vol(6) / realized_vol(100),1) < r) & (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2)) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Exit unspecified on the page; 3-day extreme exit chosen by us. realized_vol used for HV (log-return stdev).

name: Connors-Raschke HV ratio with inside day OR NR4
author: Laurence Connors / Linda Raschke
summary: Street Smarts volatility setup: 6/100 historical volatility ratio below 0.5 and the day is an inside day or an NR4, then bracket the next day's break.
long_entry: (shift(realized_vol(6) / realized_vol(100),1) < r) & ((shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) | (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2))) & close > shift(high,1)
short_entry: (shift(realized_vol(6) / realized_vol(100),1) < r) & ((shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) | (shift(high - low,1) < lowest(high - low,3,2))) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Forum thread quotes the setup; exits (book: trail, exit in a few days) approximated by a 3-day extreme break.

name: Inside day breakout with mother-bar target
author: Day Trading Toolkit
summary: Bracket the inside day; stop on the opposite side of the inside day, first target = mother bar width projected from the breakout.
short_entry: (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & close < shift(low,1)
notes: Stop at inside-day extreme approximated by 2-day low/high; mother-bar target not expressible as a fixed fraction (omitted). Intraday entry approximated by close.

name: Inside bar break with the trend only
author: LuxAlgo
summary: In an established trend, take only the inside-bar break in the trend direction with the opposite extreme as invalidation.
long_entry: (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & close > shift(high,1) & sma(close,50) > shift(sma(close,50),10)
short_entry: (shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2)) & close < shift(low,1) & sma(close,50) < shift(sma(close,50),10)
notes: Trend defined by rising/falling SMA(50) (our choice); invalidation uses a rolling 2-bar-back extreme.

name: Hikkake (failed inside-bar break)
author: Daniel L. Chesler (via LuxAlgo)
summary: After an inside bar, a false break of one side followed by a move through the opposite side is traded in the snap-back direction.
long_entry: shift(high,2) < shift(high,3) & shift(low,2) > shift(low,3) & shift(low,1) < shift(low,2) & shift(high,1) < shift(high,2) & close > shift(high,2)
short_entry: shift(high,2) < shift(high,3) & shift(low,2) > shift(low,3) & shift(high,1) > shift(high,2) & shift(low,1) > shift(low,2) & close < shift(low,2)
notes: Three-bar expiry reduced to a trigger on the bar after the false break. Invalidation beyond the false-break extreme approximated by 3-day extreme.

name: Bollinger Method I squeeze (BandWidth 6-month low) with PSAR exit
author: John Bollinger (Bollinger on Bollinger Bands)
summary: When BandWidth hits a six-month low, trade the close outside the bands; Parabolic SAR as the exit to handle head fakes.
long_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),m) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close > bb_up(close,20,2)
short_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),m) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close < bb_lo(close,20,2)
notes: m = how recently the squeeze must have occurred (our parameter). psar_dir assumed +1 up / -1 down.

name: Bollinger squeeze breakout with volume confirmation
author: TradingView author
summary: Squeeze = BandWidth below its own average; long on a close above the upper band with volume above its 20-period average, short mirror.
long_entry: ((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)) < sma(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),n) & close > bb_up(close,20,2) & volume > sma(volume,20)
short_entry: ((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)) < sma(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),n) & close < bb_lo(close,20,2) & volume > sma(volume,20)
notes: Exit not stated in the snippet; middle-band exit chosen. BandWidth-average length n unspecified.

name: Bollinger squeeze with BandWidth RSI (weekly, QS)
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Weekly bars: 10-week RSI of BandWidth below 45 and a new 5-bar closing high triggers a buy held 20 weeks; reported to perform poorly on most assets.
notes: Converted weekly to daily (10 weeks = 50 days, 5 weeks = 25 days). The 20-week time exit cannot be expressed; replaced by close < SMA(100).

name: BandWidth threshold switch (long while bands are wide)
author: SentimenTrader
summary: Buy when Bollinger BandWidth crosses above a threshold and sell when it crosses back below; vendor test on BBY 2004-2025 +436% vs +134% buy-and-hold.
notes: Vendor threshold is 10 (percent) for a stock; BTC bandwidth runs higher so 0.1-0.3 (as fraction) offered.

name: BandWidth bottom-percentile squeeze breakout
author: Stock Alarm
summary: Treat BandWidth in the bottom ~5th percentile of the past year as a high-alert squeeze and trade the close outside the bands.
long_entry: lowest(zscore(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),250),10) < z & close > bb_up(close,20,2)
short_entry: lowest(zscore(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),250),10) < z & close < bb_lo(close,20,2)
notes: Percentile rank not in vocabulary; z-score of BandWidth over 250 days used as proxy. Exit at middle band chosen by us.

name: Bollinger squeeze breakout, exit on close back inside bands
author: Trade Ideas
summary: Enter the squeeze breakout; exit (false break) as soon as price closes back inside the bands; stop on far side of the middle band.
long_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),10) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close > bb_up(close,20,2)
short_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),10) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close < bb_lo(close,20,2)
notes: Squeeze defined as 125-day BandWidth low within 10 days. 1-2x band-width targets omitted.

name: Bollinger squeeze then surge with RSI/MACD confirmation
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Squeeze breakouts suffer false breaks, so require RSI and MACD confirmation before entering the expansion.
long_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),10) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close > bb_up(close,20,2) & macd(close,12,26) > macd_signal(close,12,26,9) & rsi(close,14) > 50
short_entry: lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),10) <= lowest(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),125) & close < bb_lo(close,20,2) & macd(close,12,26) < macd_signal(close,12,26,9) & rsi(close,14) < 50
notes: Blog gives no fixed thresholds; standard MACD(12,26,9), RSI(14)>50, middle-band exit assumed.

name: Bollinger breakout held to the middle band
author: QuantConnect community
summary: Enter on a close above the upper band and hold until price touches the middle band; low win rate (26-38%) with large winners in shared crypto-era backtests.
notes: Asset of the shared backtest not stated; 20/2 bands assumed.

name: Bollinger breakout with RSI>50, 2% stop, 2:1 target (crypto)
author: TradingView author
summary: Long on a close above the 20/2 upper band with RSI above 50, short mirror; 2% stop and 2:1 reward-to-risk target, built for 4H crypto.
short_entry: close < bb_lo(close,20,2) & rsi(close,14) < 50
notes: Designed for 4H; applied to daily bars. Signal-based exits = opposite entry (backstop to stop/target).

name: Bollinger %B band-tag mean reversion
author: John Bollinger (via LuxAlgo)
summary: Use %B as a normalized overbought/oversold gauge in ranges: buy band tags below the lower band, exit as %B recovers.
notes: Page gives no thresholds; lo/hi grids are ours. Page warns trends can pin %B at extremes.

name: TTM Squeeze fire with momentum direction (Carter)
author: John Carter
summary: When Bollinger(20,2) moves back outside Keltner(20,km ATR) after a squeeze, trade in the direction of momentum and exit when momentum fades.
long_entry: shift(bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,km),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,km) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) > 0
short_entry: shift(bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,km),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,km) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) < 0
notes: Momentum histogram approximated as close minus the average of Donchian mid and SMA(20) (no linear regression). km=1.0/2.0 cover the TTM Squeeze Pro channels. kc_* assumed EMA+ATR.

name: Squeeze Momentum (LazyBear) strategy, exit on momentum sign flip
author: LazyBear (strategy port)
summary: Enter when the bands expand outside Keltner and the momentum histogram is positive (negative for shorts); exit on histogram sign change.
short_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) < 0
notes: LazyBear uses linreg momentum; approximated without regression.

name: Squeeze release with SMA-basis direction (BTCUSD)
author: PineForge
summary: On the first bar after BB(20,2)-inside-KC(20,1.5) ends, go long if close > SMA basis, short if below; no exits other than the opposite release.
short_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & close < sma(close,20)
notes: Script recommends 1h/4h; applied to daily. No stop/target in code.

name: Squeeze release only in the higher-timeframe trend direction
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Pre-assign the expected release direction from the higher-timeframe trend and take only agreeing squeeze fires, exiting as momentum wanes.
long_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) > 0 & close > sma(close,200)
short_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) < 0 & close < sma(close,200)
notes: Higher-timeframe trend approximated with SMA(200) on daily.

name: Trend crossover that stands down during squeezes
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Uses squeeze-on periods as a regime filter: trend signals are ignored while Bollinger Bands sit inside Keltner Channels.
short_entry: ema(close,20) < ema(close,50) & bb_up(close,20,2) > kc_up(20,1.5)
notes: Underlying trend system (EMA 20/50) chosen by us; source only describes the filter.

name: Squeeze fire filtered by low volatility-of-volatility
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Compression setups presume a stable quiet phase, so squeeze signals forming while volatility itself is thrashing are discounted.
long_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) > 0 & (stdev(realized_vol(20),20) / sma(realized_vol(20),20)) < sma((stdev(realized_vol(20),20) / sma(realized_vol(20),20)),100)
short_entry: (shift((bb_up(close,20,2) < kc_up(20,1.5)),1) & bb_up(close,20,2) >= kc_up(20,1.5)) & (close - ((highest(high,20) + lowest(low,20)) / 2 + sma(close,20)) / 2) < 0 & (stdev(realized_vol(20),20) / sma(realized_vol(20),20)) < sma((stdev(realized_vol(20),20) / sma(realized_vol(20),20)),100)
notes: Vol-of-vol measured as coefficient of variation of 20-day realized vol; threshold = its 100-day mean (our choice).

name: Keltner channel breakout, stop and reverse
author: StockSharp
summary: 20-period channel with 2x ATR: long when close crosses above the upper band, short when it crosses below the lower band; opposite break reverses.
short_entry: cross_below(close, kc_lo(20,2))
notes: Example used 5-minute candles; applied to daily.

name: Keltner buy above upper, sell below lower
author: Liberated Stock Trader
summary: Buy above the upper Keltner band, sell below the lower band; tested and found to win only ~28% of trades.
notes: Long only; source tested several settings.

name: Keltner original ten-day moving average rule
author: Chester Keltner
summary: Channel = 10-day SMA of typical price +/- 10-day average daily range; buy closes above the upper line, sell closes below the lower line.
long_entry: close > sma((high + low + close) / 3,10) + sma(high - low,10)
long_exit: close < sma((high + low + close) / 3,10) - sma(high - low,10)
short_entry: close < sma((high + low + close) / 3,10) - sma(high - low,10)
short_exit: close > sma((high + low + close) / 3,10) + sma(high - low,10)
notes: Always-in reversal interpretation of the 1960 rule.

name: Keltner band-touch mean reversion to EMA
author: StockSharp
summary: Buy below the lower Keltner band, short above the upper band, exit when price returns to the middle EMA.
short_entry: close > kc_up(20,k)
notes: ATR stop from the sample omitted.

name: Keltner midline pullback in trend
author: LuxAlgo
summary: In a healthy trend price travels between midline and outer band; pullbacks to the midline are continuation entries, the opposite band is the exit rail.
long_entry: ema(close,20) > shift(ema(close,20),5) & low < ema(close,20) & close > ema(close,20)
short_entry: ema(close,20) < shift(ema(close,20),5) & high > ema(close,20) & close < ema(close,20)
notes: Trend = 5-day EMA slope (our choice).

name: STARC band reversal
author: Manning Stoller / SentimenTrader
summary: Buy at the lower STARC band (short SMA minus ATR multiple) and sell near the upper band; vendor reversal backtest on COIN.
notes: Standard STARC 6-period SMA and 15-period ATR assumed.

name: STARC bands trend-side pullback
author: LightningChart
summary: In an uptrend buy near the lower STARC band and sell near the upper band; in a downtrend short the upper band and cover at the lower.
short_entry: close < sma(close,50) & close > sma(close,6) + 2 * atr(15)
notes: Trend filter SMA(50) chosen by us.

name: ATR deviation entry with positive drift (KL)
author: TradingView author (KL)
summary: Long when ATR moves one standard deviation away from its mean while the drift (expected log return) is positive; trailing stop plus 1R/2R/3R scale-outs. VOO 1h: ~46% win, 159% vs 120% B&H.
notes: Defaults not published; trailing stop modeled as 3 ATR from 10-day high close; scale-outs omitted.

name: Chandelier Exit flip system
author: Charles LeBeau (TradingView port)
summary: Long stop = 22-bar high minus 3 ATR, short stop = 22-bar low plus 3 ATR; flip direction when the close breaches the opposite stop.
short_entry: close < shift(highest(high,n) - k * atr(n),1)
notes: Ratchet (stop never loosens) not expressible; rolling stop used.

name: Chandelier Exit with EMA trend filter
author: TradingView author
summary: Chandelier flip signals taken only when an EMA filter confirms the trend.
long_entry: close > shift(lowest(low,n) + k * atr(n),1) & close > ema(close,m)
short_entry: close < shift(highest(high,n) - k * atr(n),1) & close < ema(close,m)
notes: EMA length not given in the snippet; grid is ours.

name: Chandelier Exit + ZLSMA
author: TradingView author
summary: Chandelier flips confirmed by a zero-lag least-squares moving average; author warns the backtest repaints.
long_entry: close > shift(lowest(low,n) + k * atr(n),1) & close > ema(close,m)
short_entry: close < shift(highest(high,n) - k * atr(n),1) & close < ema(close,m)
notes: ZLSMA is not in the vocabulary; replaced by EMA. Script defaults not verified (n=1 ATR period commonly cited).

name: Chandelier Exit + double RSI (BTCUSD)
author: TradingView author
summary: Stay short until the Chandelier Exit flips to buy and RSI confirms; applied to BTCUSD.
long_entry: close > shift(lowest(low,n) + k * atr(n),1) & rsi(close,7) > 50 & rsi(close,14) > 50
short_entry: close < shift(highest(high,n) - k * atr(n),1) & rsi(close,7) < 50 & rsi(close,14) < 50
notes: Chart idea only; RSI lengths/levels for the 'double RSI' assumed (7 and 14, 50 line).

name: Wilder Volatility System (ARC stop and reverse)
author: J. Welles Wilder
summary: Always-in system: SAR = significant close -/+ ARC (constant 2.8-3.1 x ATR); a close through the SAR reverses. Variants: Williams ATR(66) x sqrt(5), Elder ATR(22) x 2.5-3.5.
short_entry: close < highest(close,n,1) - k * atr(na)
notes: Significant close since entry approximated by rolling n-day extreme close.

name: Volatility Stop strategy (long only, 20/2)
author: LuxAlgo / TradingView built-in
summary: Buy when price crosses above the Volatility Stop line and close when it crosses below; built-in defaults length 20, factor 2.
notes: Stop ratchet approximated with rolling 20-day extremes; 1.75 suggested for BTC by a third party.

name: Supertrend stop and reverse
author: Olivier Seban (via LuxAlgo)
summary: Always-in system that flips with the ATR-based Supertrend line (common default 10, 3).
short_entry: supertrend_dir(n,k) < 0
notes: supertrend_dir assumed +1 up / -1 down.

name: Multiple Supertrends must agree
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Run several Supertrends with different multipliers so the binary state becomes graded; trade only when all agree.
short_entry: supertrend_dir(10,1) < 0 & supertrend_dir(11,2) < 0 & supertrend_dir(12,3) < 0
notes: The (10,1)(11,2)(12,3) triple is a popular community setting, not stated on the page.

name: Elder SafeZone stop in an EMA trend
author: Alexander Elder
summary: Trend defined by EMA slope; stop placed a multiple of the average downside penetration below the prior low.
short_entry: ema(close,22) < shift(ema(close,22),3)
notes: Elder averages only bars with a penetration; we average all 10 bars (tighter stop, adjust k). Ratchet omitted.

name: Chaikin Volatility rise-from-low / fall-from-high
author: Marc Chaikin / TrendSpider
summary: Go long when Chaikin Volatility climbs from a low level; exit when it turns down from a high level.
long_entry: shift((ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)),1) < lo & (ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)) > shift((ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)),1)
long_exit: shift((ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)),1) > hi & (ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)) < shift((ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)),1)
notes: Chaikin Volatility expressed as ratio EMA10(range)/its value 10 bars ago (=1+ROC). Levels not standardized; grids ours.

name: Chaikin Volatility spike capitulation buy
author: Marc Chaikin (via LuxAlgo)
summary: A fast spike in Chaikin Volatility during a downtrend flags capitulation that, in Chaikin's reading, can precede a bottom.
long_entry: (ema(high - low,10) / shift(ema(high - low,10),10)) > s & close < shift(close,10)
notes: Page describes context not timing; exit at SMA(20) recovery is ours.

name: Mass Index reversal bulge
author: Donald Dorsey (via LuxAlgo)
summary: Mass Index above 27 then back below 26.5 signals a trend reversal; direction taken against the 9-EMA trend.
long_entry: highest((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),10,1) > 27 & cross_below((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),26.5) & close < ema(close,9)
long_exit: highest((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),10,1) > 27 & cross_below((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),26.5) & close > ema(close,9)
short_entry: highest((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),10,1) > 27 & cross_below((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),26.5) & close > ema(close,9)
short_exit: highest((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),10,1) > 27 & cross_below((sma(ema(high - low,9) / ema(ema(high - low,9),9),25) * 25),26.5) & close < ema(close,9)
notes: Held until the next opposite bulge. Bulges are rare on BTC daily; thresholds as published.

name: Schwager volatility ratio wide-range reversal day
author: Jack Schwager
summary: A day whose true range is about 2x the recent ATR marks a candidate turning point; trade it as a reversal against the prior move.
long_entry: atr(1) > 2 * shift(atr(14),1) & close < sma(close,20) & close > (high + low) / 2
short_entry: atr(1) > 2 * shift(atr(14),1) & close > sma(close,20) & close < (high + low) / 2
notes: Direction rule (close-in-range against the prior trend) and exits are ours; the source only defines the wide-ranging day screen (ratio near 2).

name: Wide-range bar initiative breakout
author: LuxAlgo
summary: A wide-range bar closing near its extreme while clearing a level is treated as an initiative break to join.
long_entry: atr(1) > k * shift(atr(20),1) & (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.8 & close > highest(high,20,1)
short_entry: atr(1) > k * shift(atr(20),1) & (high - close) / (high - low) > 0.8 & close < lowest(low,20,1)
notes: Level = 20-day channel; exit on 10-day opposite extreme (ours).

name: ATR contraction-into-expansion transition
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Gate breakout tactics to transitions from sustained ATR contraction into expansion.
long_entry: lowest(atr(5) / atr(50),10) < c & cross_above(atr(5) / atr(50),1) & close > sma(close,20)
short_entry: lowest(atr(5) / atr(50),10) < c & cross_above(atr(5) / atr(50),1) & close < sma(close,20)
notes: ATR(5)/ATR(50) ratio and thresholds are ours; source is conceptual.

name: Expansion = trend, contraction = fade (playbook switching)
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Expansion regimes reward trend/momentum entries while contraction rewards fading range edges; a regime classifier turns that into a switch.
long_entry: (atr(5) > atr(20) & close > highest(close,20,1)) | (atr(5) < atr(20) & close < bb_lo(close,20,2))
long_exit: (atr(5) > atr(20) & close < lowest(close,10,1)) | (atr(5) < atr(20) & close > sma(close,20))
notes: Long side only; regime = ATR(5) vs ATR(20); entry/exit choices ours.

name: Donchian width compression breakout
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Normalized Donchian width in the low end of its own history marks compression; trade the subsequent channel break.
long_entry: lowest(zscore(((highest(high,20) - lowest(low,20)) / close),250),10) < z & close > highest(high,20,1)
short_entry: lowest(zscore(((highest(high,20) - lowest(low,20)) / close),250),10) < z & close < lowest(low,20,1)
notes: Percentile replaced by z-score; exits ours.

name: Fractal dimension (FRAMA-style) trend filter
author: John Ehlers / LuxAlgo
summary: Low fractal dimension flags persistent trending stretches; near/above the random-walk zone flags chop where trend signals whipsaw.
short_entry: (2 * ((highest(high,10) - lowest(low,10)) + (highest(high,10,10) - lowest(low,10,10))) / (highest(high,20) - lowest(low,20))) < 2.639 & close < sma(close,20)
notes: D = log2((N1+N2)/N3); D<1.4 <=> ratio<2^1.4=2.639, D>1.6 <=> ratio>3.03 (thresholds ours, 20-bar window).

name: Choppiness Index trending-regime switch
author: StockSharp (CHOP by E.W. Dreiss)
summary: Only while CHOP(14) < 38.2: long above SMA(20), short below; exit when CHOP rises above 61.8; no stop or target.
short_entry: (sma(atr(1),14) * 14 / (highest(high,14) - lowest(low,14))) < 2.737 & close < sma(close,20)
notes: CHOP=100*log10(sumTR/(HH-LL))/log10(14); thresholds converted: 38.2 -> ratio 14^0.382=2.737, 61.8 -> 14^0.618=5.115.

name: Choppiness filter at 50 with MA direction (BTC)
author: TradingView author
summary: Trade with the MA direction on Bitcoin and avoid trades when the Choppiness Index is above 50.
short_entry: (sma(atr(1),14) * 14 / (highest(high,14) - lowest(low,14))) < 3.742 & close < ema(close,50)
notes: CHOP 50 -> ratio 14^0.5 = 3.742. MA length not given; EMA(50) assumed. Extra 45/25 levels ignored.

name: CHOP zone entry with DMI direction and PSAR exit
author: TradingView author
summary: Enter when choppiness shows a trending zone and DMI gives direction; exit on Parabolic SAR flip.
short_entry: (sma(atr(1),14) * 14 / (highest(high,14) - lowest(low,14))) < 2.737 & plus_di(14) < minus_di(14)
notes: Zone threshold assumed 38.2; default DMI(14), PSAR(0.02,0.2).

name: Kaufman efficiency-ratio gated breakout
author: Perry Kaufman (via LuxAlgo)
summary: Trend systems trade only while the efficiency ratio is above a threshold (e.g. 0.4) and stand aside as it decays toward zero.
short_entry: (abs(close - shift(close,20)) / (sma(abs(close - shift(close,1)),20) * 20)) > e & close < lowest(close,20,1)
notes: 20-bar ER; base breakout system and exits ours.

name: Hurst regime switch with neutral band (0.45 / 0.60)
author: TradingView author
summary: H > 0.60 = trending (trend-follow), H < 0.45 = anti-persistent (mean-revert), in between = no edge.
notes: Hurst approximated by aggregated-variance scaling: stdev(10d returns)/stdev(1d returns) = 10^H, so H>0.6 <=> ratio>3.981, H<0.45 <=> ratio<2.818. Weekly macro Hurst filter omitted; trend/MR legs are ours.

name: Hurst > 0.5 trend gate
author: TradingView author
summary: H above 0.5 indicates a trending market; below 0.5 the market is more likely to mean-revert.
notes: H via 10^H = stdev(10d)/stdev(1d) over 100 days; 0.5 <=> 3.162. Trend leg (SMA20) ours.

name: Hurst exponent mean reversion
author: StockSharp
summary: When H < 0.5 fade deviations from the moving average; vendor claims ~121% average annual return, best on crypto.
short_entry: (stdev(roc(close,10),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) < 3.162 & close > sma(close,20)
notes: Hurst approximated via return-variance scaling; vendor result unverified.

name: Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio + drift t-stat regime
author: TradingView author (after Lo & MacKinlay 1988)
summary: Variance ratio below 0.8 = mean reversion; drift t-statistic above 1.96 = significant trend.
long_entry: (((stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) * (stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) / 5) < 0.8 & close < bb_lo(close,20,2)) | (((stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) * (stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) / 5) >= 0.8 & (sma(roc(close,1),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100) * 10) > 1.96)
long_exit: (((stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) * (stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) / 5) < 0.8 & close > sma(close,20)) | (((stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) * (stdev(roc(close,5),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100)) / 5) >= 0.8 & (sma(roc(close,1),100) / stdev(roc(close,1),100) * 10) < 0)
notes: VR(5) over 100 days = (stdev 5d/stdev 1d)^2/5; t-stat = mean/stdev*sqrt(100). Trading legs ours.

name: Variance ratio > 1 trend filter
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Rolling variance ratios above 1 indicate trending behaviour, below 1 mean reversion; used as a trend-versus-reversion gauge.
notes: Underlying EMA 20/50 cross ours.

name: ADX regime switch: MA cross above 20, mean reversion below
author: CrossTrade
summary: Only run the MA crossover strategy when ADX > 20 and only run mean reversion when ADX < 20.
notes: MA lengths and the MR leg (Bollinger) are ours.

name: Bollinger mean reversion skipped when ADX > 25
author: CrossTrade
summary: Fade outer-band touches back to the 20-period middle band, skipping trades when ADX(14) > 25.
short_entry: close > bb_up(close,20,2) & adx(14) < 25

name: BB breakout above ADX 25, reversion below ADX 20
author: TradingView author
summary: ADX >= 25 enables a Bollinger breakout strategy, ADX <= 20 a reversion strategy, 20-25 no signals.
long_exit: close > bb_up(close,20,2) & adx(14) <= 20 | close < sma(close,20) & adx(14) >= 25
short_entry: (adx(14) >= 25 & close < bb_lo(close,20,2)) | (adx(14) <= 20 & close > bb_up(close,20,2))
short_exit: close < bb_lo(close,20,2) & adx(14) <= 20 | close > sma(close,20) & adx(14) >= 25
notes: Band-width agreement condition and exact exits not specified; exits ours.

name: Long while EWMA volatility below slow volatility
author: LuxAlgo
summary: EWMA volatility above a slower equal-weighted estimate says turbulence is recent and building; below it, decaying.
notes: Variance compared (squared returns) instead of volatility - same ordering. Long-only risk-on/off use is ours.

name: Mean reversion only at high volatility percentile
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Breakout systems need low volatility percentile; mean-reversion systems may trade only when the percentile is elevated.
notes: Percentile replaced by z-score; MR legs ours.

name: Ulcer Index filter on trend longs
author: Peter Martin (via LuxAlgo)
summary: Skip new longs while the Ulcer Index is elevated; a low reading confirms a low-stress trend where trend-following works.
long_entry: sma((close / highest(close,14) - 1) * (close / highest(close,14) - 1),14) < u2 & close > sma(close,50)
long_exit: sma((close / highest(close,14) - 1) * (close / highest(close,14) - 1),14) > u2 | close < sma(close,50)
notes: Ulcer Index(14)^2 compared to threshold^2 (3%, 5%, 8%) since sqrt is not in the vocabulary. Base trend rule (SMA50) ours.

name: Connors/Landry VIX Reversal III applied to BTC
author: Dave Landry / Connors Research (port)
summary: Buy when VIX closes at least 10% above its 10-day MA; exit when VIX falls below the prior day's 10-day MA.
notes: Original trades S&P; VIX-low-above-MA condition dropped (no VIX low series). Intraday exit approximated by close.

name: Connors VIX Reversal II (VIX RSI) applied to BTC
author: Larry Connors (modified port)
summary: 25-period RSI of VIX above 61 then a downtick triggers a long held 7-12 days.
notes: 7-12 day time exit not expressible; exit when VIX RSI reaches the 42 oversold level instead.

name: VIX Fix + BTC realized vol with EMA(50) gate
author: TradingView author
summary: Combines a synthetic VIX (VIX Fix) and BitMEX BVOL7D with a 50 EMA regime gate; exits when price crosses below the EMA.
long_entry: ((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100) > (sma(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20) + 2 * stdev(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20)) & realized_vol(7) > sma(realized_vol(7),30) & close > ema(close,50)
notes: BVOL7D replaced by realized_vol(7). Exact combination thresholds not stated; spike = upper Bollinger band of VIX Fix.

name: Williams VIX Fix spike roll-over buy
author: Larry Williams / ChrisMoody
summary: VIX Fix = (22-day highest close - low)/highest close; spikes above its upper band mark capitulation, confirmed when the reading rolls over.
long_entry: shift(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),1) > shift((sma(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20) + 2 * stdev(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20)),1) & ((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100) < (sma(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20) + 2 * stdev(((highest(close,22) - low) / highest(close,22) * 100),20))
notes: Exit not given by source; first new 5-day closing high used (ours).

name: SMA 25/50 cross with VIX panic threshold
author: TradingView author
summary: Long on SMA25 crossing above SMA50 while VIX is below 32; panic exit when VIX rises above 32 or on a dead cross.
notes: 3-bar MA reclaim entries and staged profit-lock stops omitted.

name: BTC long while VIX falls (sentiment-beta)
author: Quantpedia
summary: Bitcoin behaves like high sentiment-beta stocks: falling market volatility (VIX) pushes investors toward bitcoin.
notes: Trading rule derived from the paper's finding (no explicit rule in the summary).

name: VIX level as cross-asset risk gate for BTC
author: LuxAlgo
summary: VIX is used as a regime filter (defensive above a chosen band) and by crypto traders as a proxy for global risk appetite.
notes: Fixed VIX thresholds (25/30/35) are ours; the page describes gating exposure above a chosen band.

name: BTC 15-day breakout only when ADX < 25
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy BTC on a break of the 15-day high only when ADX(14) < 25 (quiet market), sell below the 15-day low; reported 90% CAGR vs 66% B&H, 63% win, 35 trades.

name: BTC trend-momentum with ATR-above-average filter
author: TradingView author
summary: EMA200 trend, Chaikin Money Flow confirmation, Stoch RSI cross out of extremes, optional ATR > its average; opposing signal closes.
long_entry: close > ema(close,200) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume,20) / sma(volume,20)) > 0 & cross_above(stoch_k(14),20) & atr(14) > sma(atr(14),20)
long_exit: close < ema(close,200) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume,20) / sma(volume,20)) < 0 & cross_below(stoch_k(14),80) & atr(14) > sma(atr(14),20)
short_entry: close < ema(close,200) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume,20) / sma(volume,20)) < 0 & cross_below(stoch_k(14),80) & atr(14) > sma(atr(14),20)
short_exit: close > ema(close,200) & (sma(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume,20) / sma(volume,20)) > 0 & cross_above(stoch_k(14),20) & atr(14) > sma(atr(14),20)
notes: Stoch RSI replaced by price stochastic (stoch_k); CMF(20) built from vocabulary; lengths are assumed defaults.

name: HV compression 'explosion potential' + Donchian break
author: TradingView author
summary: Daily setup from low HV percentile, short/long HV ratio < 1 and negative log-Z of HV; trigger on a Donchian break with bullish daily bias and expanding volatility.
long_entry: lowest(zscore(realized_vol(10),250),10) < z & realized_vol(10) / realized_vol(100) < 1 & close > ema(close,50) & close > highest(high,20,1) & ((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)) > shift(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),1)
short_entry: lowest(zscore(realized_vol(10),250),10) < z & realized_vol(10) / realized_vol(100) < 1 & close < ema(close,50) & close < lowest(low,20,1) & ((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)) > shift(((bb_up(close,20,2) - bb_lo(close,20,2)) / sma(close,20)),1)
notes: Trigger meant for 4H; done on daily. Score weights/lookbacks unpublished; exits not described (ours).

name: Buy BTC breakout after record-low realized volatility
author: Fidelity Digital Assets (via CryptoRank)
summary: BTC volatility in the bottom 1.5% of history historically preceded large moves, direction uncertain.
notes: Direction resolved by a 20-day breakout (ours); 'record low' = within 10% of 2-year min.

name: Volatility contraction pattern screener breakout
author: sharpely
summary: VCP screen: ATR14/close below a cap, ATR14 below ATR50, one-month range under 10% of price; buy the pivot break.
long_entry: atr(14) / close < a & atr(14) < atr(50) & (highest(high,21,1) - lowest(low,21,1)) / close < w & close > highest(high,21,1)
notes: Vendor thresholds for stocks (5%, 10%); wider grid for BTC. Stop under last contraction approximated by 21-day low.

name: Minervini VCP with trend template
author: Mark Minervini
summary: Inside a qualifying uptrend, successive smaller pullbacks with drying volume; buy the pivot break on expanding volume, stop under the last contraction.
long_entry: close > sma(close,50) & sma(close,50) > sma(close,150) & sma(close,150) > sma(close,200) & (highest(high,10,1) - lowest(low,10,1)) < 0.5 * (highest(high,20,11) - lowest(low,20,11)) & close > highest(high,10,1) & volume > sma(volume,50)
notes: Contraction sequence reduced to last-10-day range < half of prior 20-day range.

name: Buy BTC at deep drawdown from all-time high
author: Bitcoin Magazine Pro
summary: Past cycle bottoms came at 77-93% drawdowns from the ATH; drawdown depth used to locate bear-market bottoms.
notes: 4-year window as ATH proxy; exit at a new 4-year high is ours (source gives no exit).

name: Kaminski-Lo stop-loss / re-entry rule
author: Kathryn Kaminski, Andrew Lo
summary: Exit the risky asset when its cumulative return over a window falls below -gamma and re-enter when it exceeds +delta; adds value when returns have momentum.
notes: Original is monthly on equities with bonds as the safe asset; daily windows ~1/3/6 months.

name: Drawdown-distribution stop-loss
author: arXiv 1609.00869 authors
summary: Set stop-loss thresholds from the distribution of maximum drawdowns; stops help only in some regimes.
notes: Bayesian threshold estimation not expressible; fixed drawdown thresholds instead; re-entry on 20-day high is ours.

name: Catching Crypto Trends (Donchian ensemble, BTC leg)
author: Carlo Zarattini, Alberto Pagani, Andrea Barbon
summary: Ensemble of Donchian-channel trend models with volatility-based sizing; long-only BTC test, then a top-20 rotation with Sharpe > 1.5 and 10.8% alpha vs BTC.
notes: Ensemble collapsed to a single lookback; volatility targeting (20% annual) and rotation omitted; exit at channel midline approximates the paper's trailing stop (check paper).

name: Bitcoin volatility scaling to 30% target (Man Group)
author: Man Group
summary: Scaling BTC exposure ex-ante to 30% volatility (2012-2024) raised Sharpe by about 0.4 regardless of half-life and improved left-tail risk.
notes: Continuous position sizing by inverse volatility; binary long/flat rules cannot express it.

name: The Impact of Volatility Targeting
author: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison, Van Hemert
summary: Across 60 assets since 1926, volatility scaling cuts tail kurtosis and raises Sharpe for risk assets.
notes: Requires fractional sizing.

name: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
author: Alan Moreira, Tyler Muir
summary: Scaling factor exposure down when realized variance is high produces large alphas and higher Sharpe ratios.
notes: Inverse-variance sizing; not binary.

name: Momentum Has Its Moments (risk-managed momentum)
author: Pedro Barroso, Pedro Santa-Clara
summary: Scaling momentum by its 6-month realized volatility nearly eliminates crashes and doubles the Sharpe ratio.
notes: Cross-sectional momentum with continuous scaling.

name: Volatility-targeted EMA trend on BTC (critique)
author: Jai Tripathi
summary: BTC's EMA-trend performance is invariant across volatility regimes, so volatility-targeting de-leveraging may be misaligned for Bitcoin.
notes: Vol targeting needs sizing; EMA parameters not in the abstract.

name: Volatility Targeting Single Asset (BackQuant)
author: BackQuant
summary: Scales single-asset exposure to a volatility target.
notes: Continuous sizing.

name: Stablecoin dry-powder copula with vol targeting
author: arXiv 2603.23480 authors
summary: Copula risk model using stablecoin supply; vol-targeted at 20%/50% with Sortino >40% above benchmark.
notes: Needs stablecoin supply data and fractional sizing.

name: Suspend trading on strategy drawdown, resume at equity high
author: MultiCharts
summary: Stop a strategy when its drawdown exceeds the historical maximum and resume when shadow equity makes a new high.
notes: Needs the strategy's own equity curve, not a market series.

name: Low BTC implied volatility (BVIV < 45) buy signal
author: Cointelegraph
summary: BVIV 30-day implied vol below 45 last preceded a ~50% BTC rally.
notes: Needs options implied volatility.

name: Markov regime switching portfolio with Bitcoin
author: Mahmoudi
summary: Two-state Markov switching: bear (low mean, high vol) and bull (high mean, low vol) states drive allocation.
notes: Requires fitted Markov-switching model.

name: MSIH(3)-AR(1) regime timing for Bitcoin
author: Samırkaş
summary: Three-regime Markov model with high regime persistence suggested for timing BTC decisions.
notes: Requires model estimation.

name: Forecasting BTC volatility spikes from whale/CryptoQuant data
author: arXiv 2211.08281 authors
summary: Synthesizer Transformer predicts volatility spikes from whale transactions; trading backtests scale buys by predicted volatility.
notes: On-chain data and ML model.

name: Return and variance risk premia in Bitcoin
author: Harbourfront Quant
summary: Exploits the variance risk premium between implied and realized BTC volatility.
notes: Needs options data.

name: BTC risk premia across two volatility regimes
author: Institut Louis Bachelier working paper
summary: Bitcoin risk premia vary with two market-volatility regimes; the variance risk premium is lower in high volatility.
notes: Options-implied variance and regime model required.

name: VIX term-structure contango regime filter
author: LuxAlgo
summary: Trade risk only while the VIX futures curve is in contango, cut risk in backwardation.
notes: VIX futures curve not in the vocabulary.

name: Hurst exponent + Q-learning momentum/mean-reversion
author: Cornell Data Science authors
summary: Hurst-based switching between momentum and mean reversion raises returns (and risk); Q-learning proposed to improve it.
notes: Reinforcement learning component not expressible.

name: Generalised Hurst statistical arbitrage in crypto
author: Marmara University authors
summary: Selects crypto pairs with anti-persistent spreads (H < 0.5) for mean-reversion spread trades.
notes: Multi-asset spread trading.
